decision_context.garmin_arbitration: hold_plan after correcting LOW ACWR underload handling
decision_context.route_interpretation: Historical 3 x Twin Peaks was 160.3 minutes and load 158.6, so three cycles are durability rather than today's quality dose.
decision_context.weekly_density_rule: Keep today's work narrow so Thursday can remain the second protected MTB exposure before Saturday's run and telematch.

session.title: Kiara 2 x Twin Peaks braking-release quality
session.purpose: Use two Twin Peaks climb-descent cycles to build repeatable braking-release timing and corner-exit quality without converting the first key session into a durability test.

dose.green_gate: Two Twin Peaks cycles only: first climb and descent as the sighting/baseline, second as the quality confirmation; 90-105 minutes elapsed and two climbs/descents maximum.
dose.yellow_gate: One Twin Peaks climb/descent only, 45-70 minutes, with no speed intent.
dose.red_or_cns_block: No technical MTB. Use rest or low-consequence recovery only.
dose.climbs: Conversational RPE 3-4 / Z1-Z2 with no pushing of steep pitches, attack efforts, or threshold accumulation.
dose.descents: Descent one at roughly 65-70 percent to establish the marker; descent two at roughly 75-80 percent only if vision, grip, timing, and posture remain clean.
dose.load_cap: Expected Garmin load 70-110; session RPE no higher than 5.

session.adaptation_hypothesis: Repeating one braking marker and exit line should improve front-tyre authority, brake release, and chassis recovery through rider timing rather than greater entry speed or a setup change.
execution_rules: Use one familiar trail and one named braking-release target.
Keep bike setup, tyre pressure, cleat position, and suspension clicks unchanged.
Compare the second descent with the first; do not chase speed, jumps, novelty, Strava time, or a third Twin Peaks cycle.
Use fresh same-day readiness, CNS, radar, and trail-condition gates before starting.

expected_result.technical: The second descent preserves or improves deliberate braking, centred posture, visual width, and corner-exit timing relative to the first.
expected_result.next_day: No unusual CNS, braking, or upper-body fatigue.

stop_rules: Do not start with red physical readiness, compromised/impaired CNS status, stale evidence, active thunder, or trail conditions above the session consequence.
Stop for delayed line choice, reactive braking, narrowed vision, a near miss, or two consecutive missed release markers.
Stop when posture becomes tall, grip becomes defensive, arm/braking fatigue exceeds 4/10, or final-descent quality can no longer match the first.
The second Twin Peaks descent ends the session; a third climb or extra loop is execution drift.
